infrastructure.reason: New files that build, verify and refresh the fork; none exists upstream and none is part of the runtime wheel.

Fork-side edits to upstream-owned build and CI files (distribution packaging, fork README, test workflow scope). They stay on refresh through the merge of upstream ancestry; a conflict in one stops the refresh for manual resolution.
Upstream's publishing, benchmark and private-integration workflows moved out of the active directory so the fork never publishes to upstream's package or runs its secrets.

patches.upstream_reason: PostgreSQL dialect typing fix with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate once reduced to the PostgreSQL EXTRACT and DATE_PART cases.
patches.reason: Preserve PostgreSQL EXTRACT numeric and DATE_PART double semantics while retaining Redshift input-dependent typing.

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite date extraction lowering with typed inputs; depends on postgres-extract-return-types, so it follows that patch upstream.
patches.reason: Lower YEAR/MONTH/DAY extraction from typed DATE inputs, preserving source-aware division; reject unproved timestamp and DATE_PART lowering. Inputs of unknown type and time fields are lowered by sqlite-temporal-lowering.

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite dialect interval lowering with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate.
patches.reason: Lower typed DATE plus/minus whole DAY/HOUR/MINUTE/SECOND intervals; reject fractional, timestamp and unknown-input cases whose semantics are unproved. Month/year offsets are lowered by sqlite-temporal-lowering.
The selected upstream base includes the dialect fix; BenchBox's separate mysql-target variant is not implicitly retired.
The selected base includes the fix and subsequent upstream algorithm replacement; do not restore the older implementation.
Core source-qualified exclusions overlap upstream. The branch's broader unfinished nested-field design has not been accepted and is not claimed equivalent.
Execute translated SQL on real engines in CI, with a lazy unittest helper and a recorded gap list for platforms that have no obtainable engine.

Engine-neutral expression rewrites in a new package. The first member folds literal sum/difference BETWEEN bounds to exact decimals so engines that evaluate decimal literals as binary floats keep rows equal to a bound; the column and table gates are arguments.; date_integer_arithmetic_to_interval rewrites `date_column +/- <integer>` into a day interval for caller-named date columns; mark_date_columns types caller-named columns as DATE so the SQLite generator can lower date arithmetic and DATE_TRUNC comparisons without a schema; safe_division, deduplicate_output_aliases, unqualified_tables and flag_comparisons_to_boolean carry the adapter fix-ups (opt-in zero-divisor NULLs for BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks and ClickHouse; Databricks output alias suffixing; the table nodes a caller qualifies; TPC-DI flag columns as booleans with the column list passed in).

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite dialect temporal lowering with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate after the other SQLite date patches.
patches.reason: Lower whole month/year offsets on a DATE that cannot overflow a month end, EXTRACT of YEAR..SECOND from inputs of unknown type, and DATE_TRUNC to STRFTIME; keep month-end rollover, CAST to TIMESTAMP, time zones and other units Unsupported.

patches.upstream_reason: Self-contained DuckDB generator fix; an upstream-submission candidate.
patches.reason: Emit the ORDER BY ALL keyword in DuckDB when a dialect without it (PostgreSQL) parsed ALL as a column, instead of quoting it as a reserved word; an upstream-submission candidate that does not depend on any other fork file.
Execute the transpiled GROUP BY ALL and ORDER BY ALL on DuckDB.

Explicit Netezza, Greenplum, Vertica, DataFusion and QuestDB dialects, each a thin subclass of postgres (BenchBox substituted postgres for them), with QuestDB's generator (comma joins, DATEADD, SUBSTRING and CTE column lists written in forms QuestDB runs) in its own module; execution tests run DataFusion dialect output and the date arithmetic rewrite on real engines; the Netezza dialect reads the SQLite date idioms (see netezza-sqlite-idioms).

patches.upstream_reason: Registers dialects that exist only in the fork; there is nothing upstream could accept.
patches.reason: Register the platform dialects in the Dialects enum and the lazy-import list so Dialect.get_or_raise resolves them; ansi and standard are not dialects the fork provides. The README, already fork-edited and unowned, is left as is.

Execute the QuestDB generator's output on QuestDB and compare rows; the generator itself is in platform-dialect-modules' sqlglot/generators/questdb.py, which needs no carried patch because it edits no upstream-owned file.

patches.upstream_reason: Self-contained Databricks generator and parser fix; an upstream-submission candidate.
patches.reason: Drop ASC/DESC and NULLS FIRST/LAST from PRIMARY KEY columns in Databricks output and accept them when Databricks reads a primary key; Databricks accepts neither, and PySpark rejects them as a syntax error. An upstream-submission candidate that depends on no other fork file.

Execute the adapter rewrites on real engines: zero divisors on Postgres, DuckDB, PySpark and chDB, alias deduplication on Postgres, DuckDB and PySpark, table qualification and flag folding on Postgres and DuckDB, and Databricks primary key syntax on PySpark; the rewrites themselves are in benchbox-rewrites, which needs no further patch.

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite DATEDIFF and DATE_SUB round trip with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate.
patches.reason: Write DATEDIFF in DAY units without an unsupported warning and write DATE_SUB as DATE(x, '-N UNIT'), so day differences and relative dates round-trip to SQLite.

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite DATE offset generator fix with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate.
patches.reason: Write a whole-day offset of a DATE (DATE +/- INTERVAL n DAY) as DATE(x, 'n DAY') instead of DATETIME(x, 'n DAY'): DATETIME returns 'YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00', which sorts after the date text of a DATE column, so d BETWEEN DATETIME(.., '-30 DAY') AND .. dropped the lower boundary day (TPC-DS Q21/Q40). HOUR, MINUTE and SECOND offsets keep DATETIME; TIMESTAMP operands stay Unsupported.

patches.upstream_reason: Exact division is a BenchBox benchmark-correctness policy applied to every SQLite output (owner decision); upstream keeps source semantics.
patches.reason: Write a source division that may truncate integers (PostgreSQL and Netezza `/`) as an exact SQLite quotient: the dividend becomes CAST(x AS REAL) unless an operand is already REAL or both operands are integer by syntax (integer literals, integer CASTs, arithmetic over them), which keep the source's truncating division (postgres 2020 / 3 stays 673). So TPC-DS Q21's inv_after / inv_before no longer truncates before BETWEEN 2.0/3.0 AND 3.0/2.0. Replaces the extraction-only division resolver; nested a / b / c chains are resolved too.

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite DATE arithmetic and comparison semantics; reads mark_date_columns from the fork's benchbox package, so it needs a typed-only reduction before an upstream offer.
patches.reason: Write a DATE plus or minus a whole number as a whole-day offset (DATE(x, 'n DAY')), DATE minus DATE as a day count, and a DATE_TRUNC result compared with a DATE (=, <>, <, <=, >, >=, BETWEEN) with the DATE as its midnight timestamp text, so SQLite no longer adds the number to the text ('2000-01-01' + 5 was 2005, TPC-DS Q72's d_date > d1.d_date + 5) or compares '2020-03-01 00:00:00' with '2020-03-01'. Operands count as DATE when the tree types them: a CAST, a DATE literal, a schema, or sqlglot.benchbox.rewrites.mark_date_columns; columns of unknown type keep their source text.

patches.upstream_reason: Snowflake REGEXP_REPLACE non-capturing group rewrite with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate.
patches.reason: Snowflake regular expressions have no non-capturing groups: turn (?:...) in a literal REGEXP_REPLACE pattern into a capturing group and renumber the \N references in a literal replacement.

The Netezza parser reads the SQLite date idioms (DATE('now' [, '-N days']), JULIANDAY(a) - JULIANDAY(b), a lone JULIANDAY) as portable date nodes so every target writes its own form; execution tests run them on SQLite, DuckDB, DataFusion, chDB, PySpark, Postgres, StarRocks and Doris and run a REGEXP_REPLACE with a non-capturing group on chDB, DuckDB, DataFusion and Postgres. The parser also reads `<expr> +/- N days` as a day interval, which TPC-DS Netezza templates use. The Netezza dialect module and its tests stay in platform-dialect-modules.

DdlOptions and transpile_ddl in the benchbox package: frozen options strip primary keys, foreign keys and unique constraints, write CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE, rename column types, and add SingleStore SHARD KEY, SORT KEY and REFERENCE TABLE clauses from caller-supplied tables and columns; tests execute the stripped and unstripped schemas on SQLite, DuckDB and Postgres.

Expression rewrites for engines that reject SQL their peers accept, with every gate passed as an argument: lowercase_identifiers and decimal_zero_literals and add_query_settings for ClickHouse (division reuses safe_division), correlated_exists_to_in (fails closed on an unexpected count), add_derived_table_aliases for StarRocks and Doris, and qualify_order_by_columns for ambiguous ORDER BY columns. The Netezza `+/- N days` reading lives in netezza-sqlite-idioms' parser and is tested here.

Execute the engine rewrites: ClickHouse rewrites on chDB, EXISTS versus IN row equality and qualified ORDER BY on DuckDB, derived table aliases, reserved alias words, ANSI SUBSTRING and quoted identifiers on StarRocks and Doris, and Netezza day durations on DuckDB, chDB, StarRocks and Doris.

patches.upstream_reason: Generator flag for engines that reject GROUP BY (); a candidate.
patches.reason: A SUPPORTS_EMPTY_GROUP_BY generator flag, off for Snowflake and Spark (and Databricks, which inherits it): a global aggregate (one with an aggregate or HAVING) drops its GROUP BY (), which those engines reject, and any other GROUP BY () warns as unsupported. The DataFusion generator turns the flag off in its own file.

Engine-compatibility rewrites in sqlglot.benchbox.compat (alias inlining, column qualification by name, one-row sources for FROM-less selects, FILTER removal for BigQuery, ClickHouse and others, literal-subquery naming and VALUES, grouped scalar subqueries, ordered list aggregates) with every gate an argument, the DataFusion generator that drops an unsupported GROUP BY (), and execution tests on Postgres, DuckDB, DataFusion, PySpark and chDB.

The Netezza parser marks every `/` as exact (sqlglot/benchbox/division.py); the Netezza and Vertica generators keep their own division (Vertica's `/` already returns a NUMERIC). Netezza-sourced benchmark queries mean a quotient, as DuckDB computes it, so every target whose `/` truncates integers writes the dividend of a division that is not integer-literal-only and has no real operand as an exact type (see postgres-exact-division). The Netezza, Vertica, DataFusion and QuestDB dialect and generator edits and the unit tests live in their existing original entries; the execution test runs the TPC-DS Q21, Q78 and Q83 shapes on every engine job (SQLite, DuckDB, DataFusion, PostgreSQL, Trino, PySpark, chDB, StarRocks, Doris).

patches.upstream_reason: Calls the fork's sqlglot.benchbox.division for divisions its Netezza parser marks; a BenchBox benchmark policy that upstream has no use for.
patches.reason: The base generator's div_sql calls sqlglot.benchbox.division.make_quotients_exact for a division the Netezza parser marked, when the target dialect has TYPED_DIVISION (PostgreSQL, Redshift, T-SQL and Fabric, Presto, Trino and Athena, Teradata, Drill, Dremio), with EXACT_DIVISION_TYPE (DOUBLE; DECIMAL on PostgreSQL; DataFusion and QuestDB DOUBLE) and EXACT_MARKED_DIVISION (off for Netezza and Vertica). Integer / integer truncates on those engines, which returned 4 instead of 6 rows for TPC-DS Q21 and wrong ratios for Q78 and Q83; Redshift uses DOUBLE because a bare DECIMAL is DECIMAL(18,0). A division of integer literals keeps the source's truncating division and SQL read as one of those dialects is unchanged.

Subquery rewrites in sqlglot.benchbox.subqueries for engines that plan subqueries badly or wrongly: NOT IN to NOT EXISTS for columns the caller says are never NULL, IN over a grouped subquery to EXISTS, and decorrelation (SQLGlot's unnest_subqueries after column qualification from a caller-passed schema and comma-join to CROSS JOIN conversion, skipping subqueries correlated by anything but equality), with execution tests on Postgres, DuckDB, DataFusion and PySpark.

TableLayout and the engine clause writers behind DdlOptions.layouts and default_layout: ClickHouse ENGINE, PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, PRIMARY KEY, SETTINGS and Nullable columns; Doris and StarRocks key models, key columns, partitioning, distribution and PROPERTIES; Redshift DISTSTYLE, DISTKEY, SORTKEY and Spectrum external tables; the strip_not_null, if_not_exists, schema and table_suffix options. Tables, key columns and tuning values are arguments; tests create the tables on chDB, Doris and StarRocks and compare the created layout.

Hive-family, lakehouse and warehouse table layouts in ddl_engines.py (an original file of benchbox-ddl-engines, so no patch is needed): Spark and Databricks USING, PARTITIONED BY, CLUSTER BY, CLUSTERED BY and TBLPROPERTIES for Delta, Iceberg, Hudi, Parquet and ORC; Hive and Athena PARTITIONED BY, ROW FORMAT, STORED AS and LOCATION for external and staging tables; Trino and Presto WITH properties; Synapse DISTRIBUTION; PostgreSQL access methods and the pg_mooncake mirror statements; tests create tables on PySpark and Trino and assert the rest as golden output.

DDL parity fixes in ddl.py, ddl_engines.py and layout.py (original files of benchbox-ddl and benchbox-ddl-engines, so no patch is needed): QuestDB symbol, timestamp, designated timestamp and partition arguments and length-free QuestDB types; BigQuery table-level NOT ENFORCED keys, qualified references, dotted project.dataset schema and the table_case option; plain arrays for engines without fixed-size arrays; a layout's file format replacing the statement's USING or STORED AS; no second Redshift SORTKEY; the strip_with_properties option; SINGLESTORE_TYPE_MAP; full-length bare VARCHAR on Doris and StarRocks; BIGNUMERIC for BigQuery decimals NUMERIC cannot hold; the float_as_real option and T-SQL REAL. Tables and columns are arguments; tests create the QuestDB tables on a real QuestDB, the Spark tables on PySpark, the StarRocks table on StarRocks and the stripped PostgreSQL table on PostgreSQL, and assert BigQuery, Redshift and SingleStore as golden output.

patches.upstream_reason: Self-contained BigQuery generator fix; an upstream-submission candidate.
patches.reason: BigQuery rejects a non-default NULLS FIRST/LAST in the window ORDER BY of FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE and NTH_VALUE unless the frame is an explicit ROWS frame. The BigQuery generator drops the clause when the key is a PARTITION BY key (constant per partition, so the result is unchanged) and otherwise sorts on `key IS NULL` first so the NULL placement is kept; a query's own ORDER BY keeps its clause. An upstream-submission candidate that depends on no other fork file.

One-row sources without VALUES in compat.py (an original file of engine-compat-rewrites, so no patch is needed): drop_literal_row_source replaces the literal_subquery_to_values rewrite that wrote (VALUES (1)) AS d(c), which ClickHouse rejects, with a FROM-less SELECT, and flatten_count_of_count turns a COUNT(*) over a nested COUNT(*) (always 1) into the source row count. Tests execute every single-row spelling and both rewrites on SQLite, DuckDB, DataFusion, PySpark, chDB, PostgreSQL, StarRocks and Doris.

patches.upstream_reason: SQLite set-operation operand parenthesization fix with no BenchBox-specific behavior; a candidate.
patches.reason: SQLite rejects a parenthesised operand of UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT, so a dialect with SET_OP_PARENTHESIZED_OPERANDS off writes every parenthesised query operand as SELECT * FROM (...) (TPC-DS Q87's (SELECT DISTINCT ...) EXCEPT (SELECT DISTINCT ...) failed with a syntax error). Execution tests compare SQLite with DuckDB rows over EXCEPT, INTERSECT, UNION, ORDER BY and LIMIT operands.

expand_grouping_sets turns a select that groups by ROLLUP, CUBE or GROUPING SETS into a UNION ALL of plain GROUP BY selects (grouped expressions outside the set read NULL, GROUPING() becomes its integer, the empty set drops its GROUP BY so it keeps the one grand-total row; window functions, ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET and DISTINCT run over the union in an outer select; a shape it cannot prove equivalent is left unchanged), and expand_moments writes STDDEV, STDDEV_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, VARIANCE and VAR_POP with COUNT, SUM and SQRT. Execution tests compare SQLite with DuckDB rows over the TPC-DS Q36, Q27 and Q67 shapes, NULL group values, empty input, HAVING, CUBE, GROUPING SETS and variances of groups of zero, one and many rows.

patches.upstream_reason: Wires the fork's sqlglot.benchbox.grouping_sets modules into the SQLite generator; upstream would first need those modules.
patches.reason: The SQLite generator expands ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS and GROUPING() into a UNION ALL of GROUP BY selects before writing SQL, and writes STDDEV, STDDEV_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, VARIANCE and VAR_POP (plain aggregates only; DISTINCT, FILTER and OVER warn as unsupported) with COUNT, SUM and SQRT, which needs SQLite's math functions. TPC-DS Q5, Q14, Q17, Q18, Q22, Q27, Q36, Q39, Q67, Q70, Q77, Q80 and Q86 return DuckDB's rows on SQLite.

Warehouse layouts in ddl_engines.py and layout.py (original files, so no patch is needed): BigQuery PARTITION BY (a DATE column, DATE(), TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(), DATETIME_TRUNC(), DATE_TRUNC(), RANGE_BUCKET(), _PARTITIONDATE), CLUSTER BY (at most four clusterable columns) and OPTIONS; Snowflake CLUSTER BY; Synapse index, PARTITION and multi-column HASH distribution; temporary tables keep their own name under schema, table_suffix and table_case. Layouts are validated against the statement's columns and raise ValueError for unsupported combinations; BigQuery and Synapse are asserted as text and parsed back (downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md).

reduce_list_aggregates in compat.py (an original file of engine-compat-rewrites, so no patch is needed) rewrites DuckDB LIST_SUM, LIST_AVG, LIST_TRANSFORM over LIST_ZIP and LEN of a list column (TPC-Havoc 1_v7) for Presto, Trino, Athena (REDUCE over ZIP_WITH or TRANSFORM(ZIP)), Spark and Databricks (AGGREGATE over ZIP_WITH) and BigQuery (UNNEST subselects over GENERATE_ARRAY with SAFE_OFFSET). Tests execute DuckDB against PySpark for Spark and Databricks and against Trino for the Presto family, with NULL elements, an all-NULL list and an uneven zip; BigQuery runs as its text transpiled to DuckDB (an engine gap) plus golden text.

Rewrites that replace the TPC-DS runner overrides in BenchBox, in original files (so no patch is needed): nullif_zero_divisors in rewrites.py (Q90 divisor pmc, every dialect), inline_order_by_aliases in compat.py (Q36, Q70, Q86 on PostgreSQL), alias_qualified_projections (Q47, Q57) and qualify_alias_shadowed_columns (Q66) in engine_rewrites.py for ClickHouse. Tests run the real queries on DuckDB, PostgreSQL and chDB with inline rows and assert each engine rejects the unrewritten text (downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md).

decimal_division_to_double in engine_rewrites.py (an original file, so no patch is needed) casts the dividend of every division to DOUBLE for ClickHouse, which truncates decimal quotients to the dividend's scale. Tests run TPC-DS Q36 and Q66 on chDB against DuckDB with quotients that do not fit two decimals, and assert the truncated rows differ without the rewrite (downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md).

use_nulls_for_rollups in engine_rewrites.py (an original file, so no patch is needed) sets group_by_use_nulls = 1 on ClickHouse queries with ROLLUP, CUBE or GROUPING SETS so rolled-up keys are NULL, not '' or 0. Tests run a Q5-shaped rollup and TPC-H Q6 with fold_between_literal_arithmetic on chDB against DuckDB (downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md).

round_inputs_to_decimal in rewrites.py (an original file, so no patch is needed) casts the input of every ROUND to DECIMAL so PostgreSQL rounds one-argument doubles half away from zero as DuckDB does and accepts a scale on columns of unknown type. Tests run the FlightData ROUND shapes on DuckDB and PostgreSQL, and assert the unrewritten PostgreSQL rows differ (downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md).
